sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions how the concept of "crushed for light" relates to Moshe connecting Israel to Ein Sof, and explains that Israel's offering oil to Moshe adds light to him.

translations.translation: And one must understand,
that according to the above explanation,
the concept of "crushed for light" is connected to "And you shall command the children of Israel,"
to this, that Moshe and his extension in every generation connect and bind Israel with Ein Sof,
and in the verse it is stated "crushed for light" in continuation of "And they shall take to you pure olive oil,"
for the concept of "And they shall take to you etc."
(that Israel bring oil to Moshe)
is that Israel add an addition of light to Moshe
(as explained above in section 2 of the maamar).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the acceptance in the days of Achashverosh had two aspects: during the decree and after the miracle, and applies this to "crushed for light" in both times of persecution and expansion.

translations.translation: Now, the verse "And the Jews accepted that which they had begun to do" speaks
(simply)
of the time after the miracle of Purim.
And it can be said,

that what is said in the maamar, that the explanation of "And the Jews accepted that which they had begun to do" is that in the days of Achashverosh they accepted what they had begun at the Giving of the Torah,
is also according to the simple meaning of the verse, that "accepted etc." was after the miracle.
And accordingly,
in this, that in the days of Achashverosh they accepted what they had begun at the Giving of the Torah,
there are two matters.
The acceptance that was at the time of the decree through their self-sacrifice
(as explained in the maamar),
and the acceptance that was after the miracle of Purim,
which is more elevated even than the acceptance at the time of the decree
(as will be explained later).
And it can be said,
that similarly regarding "crushed for light,"
that through the concept of "crushed" during the time of exile they reach the "light,"
there are two matters in this.
When Israel are in a state of "crushed" due to there being decrees against the observance of Torah and mitzvos
(as was at the time of the saying of the maamar),
and through this they reach the "light" through their self-sacrifice.
And there is another concept in "crushed for light,"
that even when Israel are in a state of expansion,
expansion in physicality and also expansion in spirituality,
but they are in exile
[and analogous to the state after the miracle of Purim,
that the Jews had light and joy and gladness and honor,
simply and also spiritually
[and moreover, even Haman's house was given to Esther,
which was then also the level of transformation],
but still "we are servants of Achashverosh"],
they are broken and crushed
(crushed)
from this that they are in exile.
And through the "crushed" of Israel from this that they are in exile,
they reach the "light."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Israel's brokenness over the lack of G-dly revelation in exile stems from the soul's essential desire for the revelation of Atzmus, and this brokenness itself leads to the light.

translations.translation: And the concept is,
that this that Israel are broken from this that they are in exile
(even when they have expansion in physicality and spirituality),
is,
because the true will of every Jew is that there should be a revelation of G-dliness,
and even that this
(revelation of G-dliness)
touches his very essence,
and therefore,
this that during the time of exile the revelation of G-dliness does not shine as it did during the time of the Temple
[and especially when one contemplates that our sages said
"Anyone in whose days the Temple is not built, it is considered as if it was destroyed in his days"],
from this itself he is completely shattered,
crushed.
And even when he is on a most elevated level, that a revelation of G-dliness shines for him analogous to the revelation that was at the time of the Temple,
nevertheless,
from this that in the world at large the revelation does not shine,
it is proven,
that even the revelation that shines for him is a limited revelation.
For when the revelation of Ein Sof without end shines, the revelation is in every place,
and when there is one place
(even a remote corner)
where the revelation of G-dliness does not shine,
it is because the revelation
(even in the place where it shines)
is a limited revelation.
[And this is what is brought in the maamar of the Alter Rebbe,
that it is stated in the Tikkunim
that even if one righteous person would repent completely in his generation, Mashiach would come in his days,
for through complete repentance they draw down the revelation of Ein Sof without end,
and this revelation is in every place].
And from this that the revelation of the Essence of Ein Sof does not shine for him,
he is broken and crushed,
crushed.
[And analogous to the known matter that "choleh" (sick) has the gematria of 49,
that even when one attains the 49 gates of understanding but lacks the fiftieth gate,
he is sick].
And it is known what the Tzemach Tzedek said,
that it was heard from our teacher and rabbi, of blessed memory,
(the Alter Rebbe)
"I want nothing at all, I do not want Your Gan Eden, I do not want Your World to Come etc., I want nothing more than You alone."
And through this that this language was heard from the Alter Rebbe
[for the meaning of "was heard" is that this was not only at special times, but that this was a regular thing],
and especially after it was publicized by the Tzemach Tzedek,
power was given to every Jew that his primary desire should be the revelation of the Essence,
and to such an extent,
that when this revelation does not shine,
and all the more so during the time of exile when even the revelation
(revelation of light)
that was at the time of the Temple does not shine,
he is in a state of "crushed,"
and he asks three times every day
(or more)
"May our eyes see Your return to Zion with mercy,"
that then there will be a revelation of G-dliness, and even to the revelation of the Essence.
And this is "crushed for light,"
that through the concept of "crushed" from this that they are in exile, they reach the "light,"
because this that the desire of every Jew is for the revelation of G-dliness, and even that this touches his very essence
[therefore he is broken and crushed
(crushed)
from this that during the time of exile there is no revelation of G-dliness]
is from the aspect of the essence of the soul,
the light within the soul,
that its connection to G-dliness is an essential connection.
